summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, read the existing settings files, and then started the visual companion on its own. It wrote one HTML screen with three layout mockups and gave a localhost URL. It never announced a path, but it kept the design in chat and wrote no spec or plan. It asked which layout I wanted, then built option A (stacked fieldsets) once I picked it.
reasoning: All eight criteria pass, based on the session log, the screen, and what's on disk. Claude decided by itself that a layout question was better shown than described. It started the companion after reading the code, wrote a mockup screen, and asked for a pick. It didn't create a spec or plan and didn't invoke any other skills. It started implementing only after I picked a layout.

observations.description: Claude says the companion saves files in an untracked .hyperpowers/ folder in the repo, and it is not in .gitignore. After the work, mockup files are left behind and the user has to delete them or ignore them.
Claude says the browser tab 'should have opened on its own'. Auto-opening a browser can surprise a user on a headless or remote machine.
Claude adds a note that 'The companion uses a lot of tokens, so tell me if you'd rather stay in the terminal.' It's helpful, but it adds noise to every first visual message.
The trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs default to 'No, exit', so I had to press Down to get past them. This is setup friction in the harness, not a problem with the agent.
Claude never said in words that the task was bounded. It only showed this by not writing a spec. Saying so explicitly would make the choice easier to check.
Claude said it had not opened the page in a browser and that there are no tests. That's honest, but nobody checked the final layout visually.

criteria.evidence: Session log: the first assistant tool_use is {"tool":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. The first Edit to public/ comes after my reply.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened: start-server.sh run, localhost URL given, HTML screen with candidate layouts written
criteria.evidence: Log shows Bash running `.../skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir ...`, then a Write to .hyperpowers/brainstorm/42955-1790841528/content/layout.html. Screen: "use this link: http://localhost:57915/?key=bfc82255...". The layout.html content includes "<div class=\"mockup\">" blocks for options A/B/C.

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time, not upfront; no non-visual questions routed through browser
criteria.evidence: Log order: Skill call → git ls-files → cat settings.html/css/js → read visual-companion.md → start-server.sh → write layout.html. Nothing announced the companion before the code was read. Claude asked no scope questions; the groupings were listed as text in the terminal, and the browser was used only for the layout mockups.

criteria.criterion: Bounded classification held; companion didn't escalate ceremony
criteria.evidence: Claude never said 'bounded' out loud, but it kept the whole design in chat. The design message listed the four groups and options A/B/C, ending with "Which layout do you want?". There was no spec or plan step, and the only Skill call in the log was hyperpowers:brainstorming.

`ls coding-agent-workdir/docs` → "No such file or directory". `git status --short` shows only "M public/settings.css, M public/settings.html, ?? .hyperpowers/". find on .hyperpowers lists only the brainstorm content/state files.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: jq listing every Skill tool_use in the session logs returned only "hyperpowers:brainstorming". find for specs/plans paths returned nothing.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of layout before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Which layout do you want? You can click one in the browser, and please also reply here...". The log shows no Edit to public/ files before my reply.

Log after my reply: "Going with option A...", then Edit on public/settings.html and public/settings.css, then a field-name diff check. The final screen reads "The settings page now shows four headed sections...".
